topics.name: Adverbs of manner, time and frequency

options: The mirror hangs on the pink wall.
The mirror hang on the pink wall.
The mirror hanging on the pink wall.
questions.rule: A singular subject (the mirror) takes a verb with -s in the simple present: hangs.

options: The mirror shows faces truthful.
The mirror shows faces truthfully.
The mirror show faces truthfully.
questions.rule: An adverb tells how something is done: shows faces truthfully.

options: The lake is more deep than the pond.
The lake is deepest than the pond.
The lake is deeper than the pond.
questions.rule: Short adjectives add -er to compare two things: deeper than.

options: looking
looks
have

questions.rule: Riya = she, so the simple present verb takes -s: looks.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: slowly
slowness
slows

questions.rule: To describe how she walked, use the adverb slowly.

options: isn't it?
is it?
doesn't it?
questions.rule: Positive sentence with is → negative tag with isn't: isn't it?

options: brighter
brightest
bright
questions.rule: Comparing two things with than needs the comparative: brighter.
She + verb with -s: She looks into the mirror.
The adverb of manner happily comes after the verb smiled.

chat: You saw the old mirror at Nani's house, didn't you?
options: Yes, I did. It was very big.
Yes, I done. It was very big.
Yes, I did. It were very big.
questions.rule: Answer a didn't you? tag with Yes, I did. It takes was.

options: The lake is calm, is it?
The lake is calm, isn't it?
The lake is calm, doesn't it?
questions.rule: Positive statement → negative tag, using the same helping verb: is → isn't it?

options: She looks always in the mirror before school.
She always looks in the mirror before school.
She always look in the mirror before school.
questions.rule: Adverbs of frequency like always come before the main verb: always looks.

options: This mirror is better than the old one.
This mirror is more better than the old one.
This mirror is gooder than the old one.
questions.rule: Good is irregular: good, better, best. Never 'more better'.

options: flickering

questions.rule: Two tall candles is plural, so the verb has no -s: flicker.

options: faith
faithfully

questions.rule: How does it reflect? Use the adverb faithfully.

options: replace
replacing
replaces
questions.rule: Her face is singular, so the verb takes -s: replaces.

questions.rule: Of all compares more than two, so use the superlative: the clearest.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a question tag.
questions.rule: Positive statement in the simple present → don't you?
Comparative + than: bigger than yours.

options: She are combing her hair in front of the mirror.
She is comb her hair in front of the mirror.
She is combing her hair in front of the mirror.
questions.rule: She takes is, and the continuous needs -ing: is combing.

options: The girl with two candles stand near the lake.
The girl with two candles standing near the lake.
The girl with two candles stands near the lake.
questions.rule: The subject is the girl (not 'candles'), so the verb is singular: stands.

options: The mirror doesn't lie, does it?
The mirror doesn't lie, doesn't it?
The mirror doesn't lie, is it?
questions.rule: Negative statement → positive tag with the same helper: doesn't → does it?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: clearest
clear
clearly

questions.rule: The ... I have ever seen compares with everything, so use the superlative: clearest.

questions.rule: How does she speak? Use the adverb softly.

options: never
ever
not
questions.rule: The adverb of frequency never goes before the verb. 'Not' needs 'does': does not tell.

options: doesn't she?
isn't she?
don't she?
questions.rule: Lives (simple present, she) → tag with doesn't she?
The adverb quickly can come before the verb; it never goes between the verb and its object.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a question tag.
questions.rule: Negative statement (didn't) → positive tag: did she?

chat: Which is brighter, the moon or a candle?
options: The moon is much more brighter than a candle.
The moon is much brightest than a candle.
The moon is much brighter than a candle.
questions.rule: Much can make a comparative stronger: much brighter. Never 'more brighter'.

chat: How did you do in the recitation contest?
options: I did good, but Meera spoke more clearly.
I did well, but Meera spoke more clear.
I did well, but Meera spoke more clearly.
questions.rule: Verbs need adverbs: did well, spoke more clearly.

options: Every morning, the woman come to the mirror.
Every morning, the woman comes to the mirror.
Every morning, the woman coming to the mirror.
questions.rule: A daily habit takes the simple present; the woman is singular: comes.

options: Mira is youngest girl in her family.
Mira is the youngest girl in her family.
Mira is the most young girl in her family.
questions.rule: The superlative needs the, and short adjectives add -est: the youngest.

questions.after: crying when her mother came in.
options: quiet
quietly

questions.rule: An adverb describes the verb crying: was quietly crying.
Long adjectives use more to compare: more important than.

chat: It's a lovely old mirror, isn't it?
options: Yes, it is. It belonged to my grandmother.
Yes, it is. It belong to my grandmother.
Yes, it does. It belonged to my grandmother.
questions.rule: Answer an isn't it? tag with it is. Past fact: belonged.

options: My sister and I use it every day.
My sister and I uses it every day.
My sister and me use it every day.
questions.rule: Two subjects joined by and are plural: use. As a subject, say I, not 'me'.

chat: Do you visit the lake often?
options: Yes, we every Sunday go there.
Yes, we goes there every Sunday.
Yes, we go there every Sunday.
questions.rule: Time phrases like every Sunday go at the end; we takes go.

options: The lake reflects the trees as clear as a mirror does.
The lake reflects the trees as clearly as a mirror does.
The lake reflects the trees as clearly than a mirror does.
questions.rule: As ... as shows equality; it describes the verb, so use the adverb: as clearly as.

options: Nothing in the room escape the mirror's eye.
Nothing in the room escapes the mirror's eye.
Nothing in the room escaping the mirror's eye.
questions.rule: Nothing is singular, so it takes a verb with -s: escapes.

options: most

questions.rule: With three or more things, use the superlative: the most beautiful.

shall we?

options: most honest
honestest

questions.rule: In the whole palace needs the superlative; honest uses most: the most honest.
Hardly ever (almost never) goes before the main verb: hardly ever shows.

chat: A mirror can't lie, can it?
options: No, it can. It shows things just as they are.
No, it can't. It show things just as they are.
No, it can't. It shows things just as they are.
questions.rule: Short answer: No, it can't. It takes shows.

chat: Which of these photos do you like?
options: The one with the two girls look the happiest.
The one with the two girls looks the happiest.
The one with the two girls looks the most happiest.
questions.rule: The subject is the one (singular): looks. Never 'most happiest'.

options: The bus was moving very slow because of the rain.
The bus was moved very slowly because of the rain.
The bus was moving very slowly because of the rain.
questions.rule: Slowly describes how the bus was moving, so use the adverb.
